findings.claim: The bundle covers no failed or incomplete export. A member whose export request fails, or who receives a truncated file, has no described observable outcome, and the failure case is neither in scope nor excluded. For a capability whose stated user value is offline analysis, silently receiving an incomplete dataset is a material product risk, because the member cannot tell a partial file from a complete one.

The bundle states no boundary on the size of an exportable filtered result. The export is defined purely as 'exactly those authorized records' with no upper bound and no described behavior when the filtered result is larger than the product intends to serve in one on-demand download. This leaves the scope boundary incomplete in the one dimension a filter-driven export can grow without limit.

The manifest's scenario links are incomplete and internally inconsistent. Two relations that hold for all three scenarios are recorded for only two of them. The declared graph therefore understates real dependencies, which is a defect in the reviewed inventory the confirm gate and any later trace view are built on.

Round-one finding: the bundle covered no failed or incomplete export, so a member could not distinguish a truncated file from a complete one. The new revision adds an observable failure branch. The finding is resolved.

The attribution of that new position is a separate defect recorded as PR-DISC-001-004; it does not reopen this finding.

Round-one finding: two manifest relations that hold for all three scenarios were declared for only two of them, so the declared graph understated real dependencies. Both missing edges are now declared. The finding is resolved.

The two new product boundaries introduced by this revision — no product-level record-count cap, and a distinguishable failure outcome for an incomplete export — are producer positions, not test-supervisor inputs, but they are recorded under the heading 'Confirmed boundaries' in a list whose closing bullet attributes the list to the test supervisor, and they are asserted without attribution in the manifest 'scope' field that the content revision hashes. A test supervisor who accepts this revision would accept product commitments they were never asked about and never made.

This revision retracted the populated-result column order without replacing it, so the bundle now fixes the CSV column order only for the degenerate empty result. Two exports of the same capability may therefore present different column orders, which defeats the stated user value of taking the records into an offline analysis tool.
